verses.zh: （上行之诗。）耶和华啊，我从深处向你求告！
verses.en: A song of ascents.[NOTE:1] From the deep water[NOTE:2] I cry out to you, O Lord.
notes: Psalm 130. The psalmist, confident of the Lord’s forgiveness, cries out to the Lord for help in the midst of his suffering and urges Israel to do the same.

The precise significance of this title, which appears in Pss 120-134, is unclear. Perhaps worshipers recited these psalms when they ascended the road to Jerusalem to celebrate annual religious festivals. For a discussion of their background see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 219-21.

verses.zh: 主啊，求你听我的声音！愿你侧耳听我恳求的声音！
verses.en: O Lord, listen to me.[NOTE:1] Pay attention to[NOTE:2] my plea for mercy.
notes: Heb “depths,” that is, deep waters (see Ps 69:2, 14; Isa 51:10), a metaphor for the life-threatening danger faced by the psalmist.

verses.zh: 主―耶和华啊，你若究察罪孽，谁能站得住呢？
verses.en: If you, O Lord, were to keep track of[NOTE:1] sins,O Lord, who could stand before you?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “may your ears be attentive to the voice of.”

verses.zh: 但在你有赦免之恩，要叫人敬畏你。
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] you are willing to forgive[NOTE:2] so that you might[NOTE:3] be honored.[NOTE:4]
notes: The words “before you” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The psalmist must be referring to standing before God’s judgment seat. The rhetorical question expects the answer, “No one.”

verses.zh: 我等候耶和华，我的心等候；我也仰望他的话。
verses.en: I rely on[NOTE:1] the Lord.I rely on him with my whole being;[NOTE:2] I wait for his assuring word.[NOTE:3]

verses.zh: 我的心等候主，胜于守夜的，等候天亮，胜于守夜的，等候天亮。
verses.en: I yearn for the Lord,[NOTE:1] more than watchmen do for the morning,yes, more than watchmen do for the morning.[NOTE:2]

verses.zh: 以色列啊，你当仰望耶和华！因他有慈爱，有丰盛的救恩。
verses.en: O Israel, hope in the Lord,for the Lord exhibits loyal love[NOTE:1] and is more than willing to deliver.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “more than watchmen for the morning, watchmen for the morning.” The words “yes, more” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “for with the Lord [is] loyal love.”

verses.zh: 他必救赎以色列脱离一切的罪孽。
verses.en: He will deliver[NOTE:1] Israelfrom all their sins.[NOTE:2]

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This is one of those Psalms that speaks to the deepest desires and hopes of faithful followers.

- there are problems, sins, and disappointments

- the believer cries out to his/her only hope, YHWH

- He hears and forgives

- He is faithful to His character and word even when humans are not (cf. Ps. 51:1)

- There are several names for Israel's Deity used in the Psalm.

- YHWH, Ps. 130:1,5,7 (twice)

- Yah, Ps. 130:3 (abbreviation of YHWH)

- Adon, Ps. 130:3,6

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD (Adon and Kurios)

- This Psalm expresses both individual and corporate yearning for restoration (cf. Psalm 130:7-8).

- Notice the grammatical theological emphasis of Ps. 130:7-8.

- Ps. 130:7, "abundant redemption" (BDB 915 I, KB 1176, Hiphil INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE)

- He (and He alone) will redeem ‒ PERSONAL PRONOUN added to VERB for emphasis

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 130:1-4

1Out of the depths I
have cried to You, O Lord.

2Lord,
hear my voice!

Let Your ears be attentive

To the voice of my
supplications.

3If You, Lord, should mark iniquities,

O
Lord, who could stand?

4But there is
forgiveness with You,

That You may be feared.

130:1 "Out of the depths" This NOUN (BDB 771) has several figurative uses. It basically means "deep."

- distress described as a flood of waters, cf. Ps. 69:1-2,14-15 (similar imagery to Ps. 42:7a; 88:7)

- YHWH as champion of watery chaos, cf. Isa. 51:9-10 (similar to Ps. 74:12-17; 89:9-10)

- the defeat of Tyre's sea power (i.e., sunk into the sea), cf. Ezek. 27:34

- possibly a reference to Sheol, cf. Jonah 2:2-6; Ps. 18:4-5; 69:2,14-15)

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEOL

▣ "I have cried to You" The exact nature of the psalmist's distress is not stated but it is related to his sense
of sin (cf. Ps. 130:3-4). He feels alienated but knows God will forgive and restore a repentant, patient follower (cf. Ps. 130:5-6)!

130:2 This verse reflects the psalmist's prayer mentioned in Ps. 130:1.

- hear ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE

- let Your ears be attentive ‒ BDB 224, KB 243, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

130:3-4 Several English translations make these two verses a separate strophe (i.e., NKJV, NRSV, NJB).

The reality of the sinfulness of all humans after the Fall of Genesis 3 is a recurrent truth throughout the Bible.

- Genesis 3:17-19; 6:5,11-12; 8:21

- 1 Kings 8:46

- 2 Chronicles 6:36

- Ezra 9:15

- Job 4:17; 9:2; 15:14-16; 25:4

- Psalm 51:5; 76:7; 130:3; 143:2

- Proverbs 20:9

- Ecclesiastes 7:20

- Isaiah 53:6

- Nahum 1:6

- Malachi 3:2

- Romans 3:9-18,19,23; 11:32

- 1 John 1:8-10

- Revelation 6:17

All need forgiveness! Humans do not sense a need for forgiveness until the Spirit clearly reveals
our need. There is no need for a savior until there is a sense of lostness! See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FORGIVENESS IN THE OLD TESTAMENT.

Forgiveness is possible because of

- the gracious, unchanging character of God (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD [OT])

- the finished work of the Messiah (cf. Isaiah 53; Mark 10:45; 2 Cor. 5:21)

- the drawing, wooing of the Spirit (cf. John 6:44,65; 16:8-15)

130:3 "mark" This VERB (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERFECT) denotes,
in this context, the preserving of a record. This is reflected in the "two books" of God (i.e., book of deeds/remembrances
and the book of life, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO BOOKS OF GOD. This is imagery for the memory of God.

It is ironic but God is asked again and again to forget our sins (i.e., Ps. 79:8; 106:6; Isa. 64:9; Micah 7:18)
but remember His promises. On Judgment Day the books will be opened (cf. Dan. 7:10; Rev. 20:12)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO BOOKS OF GOD

▣ "who could stand?" This implies a court scene with YHWH as the righteous judge (cf. Ezra 9:6,15; Ps. 76:7;
Nahum 1:6; Mal. 3:2; Rev. 6:17).

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGMENT IN THE NT

130:4 "feared" The outcome of a free and full forgiveness by a gracious God is the restoration of the personal
relationship with God (i.e., lost in the Fall of Genesis 3), which is/was/will be the goal of creation. We were created by Him
and for Him. Fear is the appropriate awe that He is due. Forgiveness results in fellowship!

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 130:5-8

5I wait for the Lord, my soul does wait,

And in His word do I hope.

6My soul waits
for the Lord

More than the watchmen for the
morning;

Indeed, more than the
watchmen for the morning.

7O Israel, hope in
the Lord;

For with the
Lord there is lovingkindness,

And with Him is abundant
redemption.

8And He will redeem
Israel

From all his iniquities.

130:5-8 This strophe emphasizes the theme of the patience of faithful followers in God and trust in His
word (cf. Ps. 130:5). The concept of "waiting in faith" is expressed in this strophe by two words.

- BDB 875, KB 1082 ‒ Ps. 130:5 (twice) and assumed in Ps. 130:6, cf. Ps. 25:3,21; 27:14; 40:1; 56:7

- BDB 403, KB 407 ‒ Ps. 130:5,7, cf. Ps. 38:15; 42:5; 43:5

This is the place where the sovereignty of God intercedes the required volitional response of fallen
mankind. Faithful followers choose to wait, hope, trust in God and His promises, even when circumstances and feeling
scream to take a different path!

130:6 This imagery for the longing anticipation is similar to Ps. 42:1-2. God's people long for Him!

▣ "soul" See full note at Gen. 35:18 online at
www.freebiblecommentary.org.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

130:7 As the psalmist longs, waits, hopes, and trusts in YHWH, he now calls on God's people collectively
to do the same.

Notice how YHWH is characterized.

- in Him is lovingkindness (i.e., covenant, loyal love, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS [hesed])

- in Him is "abundant redemption" (Ps. 130:7c)

- in Him (and no other, cf. REB) is redemption (NOUN in Ps. 130:7 and VERB in Ps. 130:8,
see SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM)
for all those who trust in Him (i.e., the covenant people, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT and
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN)

Remember biblical faith is corporate. It is a family! Be careful of the modern western over-emphasis
on the individual. Salvation has a corporate focus! We are saved to serve. The goal of individual salvation is the health
and growth of the body of believers!

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL FAITH IS CORPORATE

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What feelings come to your mind/heart after reading Ps. 130:1-4?

- What do you think "depths" means?

- Does God keep a record of sins?

- Does Ps. 130:5-6 describe how you feel about God and His word?
